title: Arctic summer extent had little link to next March extent in 45 seasons from 1979 to 2023
abstract: We tested seasonal sea ice recovery with 45 summer-to-winter pairs per pole from Sea Ice Index Version 4. After linear trend removal, the Arctic winter-on-summer slope was -0.031, with a conditional 95 percent three-season block interval of -0.168 to 0.110. The summer-to-winter-gain correlation was -0.902. The gain slope equals the endpoint slope minus one, so this strong negative link does not by itself show a physical recovery feedback. Adding summer extent increased later-year Arctic winter forecast RMSE from 0.312 to 0.324 million square kilometres. The Antarctic endpoint slope was 0.442 in the full record but -0.137 when the record ended in 2015. Both block intervals included zero. Extent alone cannot identify heat or thickness processes. The package gives fixed endpoint evidence, source hashes, code, uncertainty, forecasts and figures.

display.caption: Winter endpoint memory and winter gain give different relations with summer extent after linear trend removal.
The Antarctic endpoint slope depends on the record end year.
